decisions.content:
# ADR-0001 Truth Model And Status Boundary

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

Previous harness documentation mixed three different statements:

- what the runtime currently does
- what the team originally intended
- what the production target should become

That made review and recovery harder.

## Decision

Harness documentation must explicitly label statements as one of:

- current reality
- known nonconformance
- target requirement

Documentation truth order is:

1. runtime code
2. systemd units
3. observed logs and status output
4. tests as intent evidence
5. earlier documentation

## Consequences

- future docs must not describe a planned state as if it is already live
- current faults must remain visible until they are removed from code and runtime
- Structurizr views must model current runtime topology, not aspirational topology
decisions.title: ADR-0001 Truth Model And Status Boundary

decisions.content:
# ADR-0002 Authoritative Claim And Dispatch

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

The current runtime allows more than one component to discover and dispatch runnable Linear work:

- webhook receiver
- backlog reconciler
- runner self-pick behavior

A lease is acquired too late to prevent duplicate dispatch.

## Decision

Per repository, one scheduler will own the transition:

- `eligible -> claimed`

That claim must be atomic and durable.

Ingress may create desired work and dedupe deliveries.

Executors may only execute already-claimed work.

## Consequences

- webhook receiver no longer grants ownership
- reconciler no longer directly dispatches runnable work
- runner no longer self-picks global runnable work
- duplicate dispatch becomes observable as rejected claim attempts rather than double execution
decisions.title: ADR-0002 Authoritative Claim And Dispatch

decisions.content:
# ADR-0003 Executor Pool And Worktree Boundaries

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

The current platform uses eight long-lived worktrees:

- `wt1` to `wt4` for Linear
- `wt5` to `wt8` for Discord

That pool split is useful, but worktrees are currently overloaded as sandboxes, durable owners, repair surfaces, and branch identities.

## Decision

Keep worktrees as executor sandboxes.

Do not use worktrees as the durable source of task truth.

Active sandboxes must not be background-mutated by recovery or unrelated synchronization.

## Consequences

- idle sandboxes may refresh from `origin/main`
- active sandboxes stay pinned to claim base until completion or expiry
- recovery may quarantine or reprovision a sandbox
- recovery may not commit, push, merge, or reset an active sandbox
decisions.title: ADR-0003 Executor Pool And Worktree Boundaries

decisions.content:
# ADR-0004 Repo-Serial Integration And Candidate Admission

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

Current execution allows parallel mutation but discovers many conflicts late, during cherry-pick integration.

The integrator is already single-writer by intent, but candidate admission rules are not explicit enough.

## Decision

Every mutating execution attempt must emit a candidate record that includes:

- repo
- job
- claim
- base SHA
- candidate SHA or patch identity
- changed paths
- validation summary

Integration is serialized once per repository.

Only the integrator may write the repository mainline.

## Consequences

- late conflict becomes an explicit candidate state
- base drift is handled through stale-base or conflict policy
- executors do not push to mainline
- merge-back remains parallel in execution but serial in admission
decisions.title: ADR-0004 Repo-Serial Integration And Candidate Admission

decisions.content:
# ADR-0005 State-Only Recovery And Divergence Policy

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

The prior recovery daemon released leases, retried pushes, auto-committed dirty work, synced worktrees, and could propagate changes after mainline repair.

That made recovery a second git writer.

## Decision

Recovery is limited to state repair, quarantine, reprovision request, stale-claim handling, and tightly bounded sandbox maintenance for inactive diverged worktrees.

Divergence is resolved by sandbox disposal or explicit replan, not by hidden background publication of work.

## Consequences

- no recovery `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `git merge` anywhere in the daemon
- no recovery auto-commit or auto-push
- no recovery reset of active worktree
- sandbox reset of inactive diverged worktrees is allowed as non-publishing maintenance
- baseline health checks detect failures and report them for operator intervention
- divergence becomes a visible state transition
decisions.title: ADR-0005 State-Only Recovery And Divergence Policy

decisions.content:
# ADR-0006 Observability, Audit, And Evidence Contract

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

Current logs are good enough to infer failure patterns but not strong enough to prove one end-to-end execution chain cleanly.

## Decision

Every job must have stable IDs across ingress, claim, execution, recovery, and integration.

Every mutating candidate must record validation and integration evidence.

Every recovery action must be provably state-only.

## Consequences

- correlation IDs alone are not enough
- claim IDs and execution attempt IDs become mandatory
- integration candidate IDs become mandatory
- operator review becomes faster and more trustworthy
decisions.title: ADR-0006 Observability, Audit, And Evidence Contract

decisions.content:
# ADR-0007 Quality Gates And Mutating Work Admission

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-04-12

## Context

The repository already exposes meaningful gate surfaces through `package.json` scripts and the `Makefile`.

The runtime needs a clear rule for what must run before mutating work can be admitted for integration.

## Decision

Mutating work is not complete when the model returns.

Mutating work is complete only when:

- required validation commands ran
- results were recorded truthfully
- candidate metadata exists
- integration admission succeeded or conflict was recorded explicitly

The minimum harness-focused gate set is:

- `npm run typecheck:harness`
- `npm run lint:harness`
- `npm run depcruise:harness`
- `npm run test:unit`

Escalate to `make quality-harness`, `make quality-fast`, or `make quality-full` according to change scope.

## Consequences

- gate results become part of candidate evidence
- fake green merges are prohibited
- operator confidence depends on recorded commands, not narrative claims
decisions.title: ADR-0007 Quality Gates And Mutating Work Admission

sections.content:
# ANQR Harness Architecture Index

## Status

The harness is **not production safe in its current orchestration form**.

The runtime is partially implemented and actively used, but it still has structural faults:

- duplicated dispatch authority
- late lease acquisition
- long-lived mutable worktrees acting as execution sandboxes and durable task owners at the same time
- recovery logic that mutates git state
- repo integration that is serialized too late
- audit trails that are useful for inference but still weak for proof

This documentation set is written to replace mixed doctrine and partial remediation notes with one clear reference set.

## Read this set in order

1. [01-scope-status-and-truth-model.md](01-scope-status-and-truth-model.md)
2. [02-current-runtime-and-service-topology.md](02-current-runtime-and-service-topology.md)
3. [03-current-control-plane-and-flows.md](03-current-control-plane-and-flows.md)
4. [04-known-failures-and-evidence.md](04-known-failures-and-evidence.md)
5. [05-production-target-architecture.md](05-production-target-architecture.md)
6. [06-state-machines.md](06-state-machines.md)
7. [07-worktree-and-git-governance.md](07-worktree-and-git-governance.md)
8. [08-quality-gates-and-post-ai-processing.md](08-quality-gates-and-post-ai-processing.md)
9. [09-observability-and-audit.md](09-observability-and-audit.md)
10. [10-operations-runbooks.md](10-operations-runbooks.md)
11. [11-validation-and-rollout-plan.md](11-validation-and-rollout-plan.md)
12. [workspace/README.md](workspace/README.md)

## What this set governs

This set governs:

- `harness/ops/*`
- `services/systemd/*`
- `workspace.dsl`
- the worktree pool used by the executor fleet
- the control-plane contract for Discord and Linear sourced work
- post-AI validation, evidence, and merge admission

This set does not redefine the ANQR product architecture outside the harness.

## Key decisions captured here

- one repository may execute many jobs concurrently
- one repository must integrate one candidate at a time
- scheduler authority must be singular per repository
- leases are execution guards, not ingress dedupe
- worktrees are sandboxes, not the durable source of task truth
- recovery must repair state before it repairs git, and it must not mutate active execution baselines

# Scope, Status, And Truth Model

## Scope

The harness is the repository-local automation platform for ANQR. It currently covers:

- Discord sourced interactive requests
- Linear sourced issue execution
- provider routing and AI execution bridges
- queue control, reconciliation, integration, recovery, and watchdog loops
- quality gate execution and evidence generation
- operator diagnostics and support tooling

## Current status

Current status is:

- operational enough to run work
- observable enough to identify failure patterns
- not reliable enough for unattended production execution

The gap is not mainly model quality. The gap is control-plane correctness.

## Truth model

When documentation, tests, and runtime disagree, use this order:

1. committed runtime code
2. committed systemd units
3. observed logs and status outputs
4. tests as intent evidence
5. previous docs and architecture narratives

This rule exists because the current harness contains remediation-era services that were added after the original design, and those additions changed control-plane behavior.

## What must be documented as distinct concerns

Every harness document must separate:

- **current reality**
- **known nonconformance**
- **target requirement**

Those three concerns must never be blended into one statement.

## Current architectural intent

The intended operating model is:

- executors `wt1` to `wt4` serve Linear sourced work
- executors `wt5` to `wt8` serve Discord sourced work
- some requests are read-only
- some requests run commands
- some requests mutate repository content
- mutating work must pass quality gates and then merge back safely
- ancillary services exist to keep the platform healthy, not to compete with executors for control

That intent is reasonable.

The current implementation does not consistently preserve it.

## Production bar

The harness is only production ready when all of the following are true:

- an eligible job is claimed once per repository
- the claim exists before any worker starts executing
- only one component has authority to decide ownership
- active work is not invalidated by background git mutation
- merge-back is serialized per repository
- stale work is invalidated by state machine rules, not by ad hoc reset
- audit records can prove who owned work, when, on which base SHA, and why ownership changed

# Current Runtime And Service Topology

## Repository runtime roots

The current runtime roots are:

- `harness/ops/*`
- `services/systemd/*`

## Main active service surfaces

### Ingress and routing

- `services/systemd/openclaw-gateway.service`
  - OpenClaw gateway
  - default port `18789`
- `services/systemd/anqr-discord-router.service`
  - Discord request router
  - default port `18790`
- `services/systemd/anqr-linear-webhook.service`
  - Linear webhook receiver
  - default port `18795` (via `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_PORT` override; default `18791`)
- `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-router.service`
  - Symphony router
  - default port `4319`
- `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-scheduler.service`
  - authoritative scheduler
  - durable claim + dispatch into the Linear executor pool

### Execution plane

- `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-executor@.service`
  - eight executor instances
  - working directories `~/src/anqr-wt1` through `~/src/anqr-wt8`
  - ports `4321` through `4328`

### Control-plane maintenance and recovery

- `services/systemd/anqr-linear-reconciler.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-integrator.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-symphony-worktree-recovery.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-watchdog.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-worktree-health.timer`

### Supporting automation

- `services/systemd/anqr-nightly.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-nightly.timer`
- `services/systemd/anqr-rag-rebuild.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-rag-rebuild.timer`
- `services/systemd/anqr-email-ingest.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-email-ingest.timer`
- `services/systemd/anqr-linear-export.service`
- `services/systemd/anqr-linear-export.timer`
- `services/systemd/anqr-context7-mcp.service`

## Worktree pool mapping

### Linear pool

- `wt1`
- `wt2`
- `wt3`
- `wt4`

Used for:

- Linear issue execution
- mutating repository work originating from issue automation
- repository tasks that need branch publication and later integration

### Discord pool

- `wt5`
- `wt6`
- `wt7`
- `wt8`

Used for:

- Discord interactive work
- read-only questions
- command execution
- repository mutation when a Discord request is allowed to change files

## Current routing code paths

### Discord path

- `harness/ops/integrations/model/discord-request-router/*`
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-openai-bridge/*`

Current behavior:

- Discord router selects the least-loaded Discord worktree
- request cwd is rewritten toward the chosen worktree
- the router forwards the request to the executor-local bridge
- executor-local bridge performs the actual model and tool work

### Linear path

- `harness/ops/integrations/model/linear-webhook-receiver/*`
- `harness/ops/integrations/model/symphony-agent-router/*`
- `harness/ops/orchestration/linear-reconciler/*`
- `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-scheduler/*`
- `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-runner/*`

Current behavior:

- webhook receiver accepts eligible events and writes desired-work ingress
- reconciler feeds desired-work signals instead of dispatching runnable work
- the authoritative scheduler claims runnable issues, assigns worktrees, and dispatches through the router
- the router verifies scheduler-owned claims on both trigger and queue-drain paths before forwarding to executors
- runners execute assigned work only; they do not self-pick global Linear work

That means the Linear path now has one effective scheduler for global issue admission and claim.

## State and persistence

Current state is file-backed through:

- `harness/ops/core/symphony-state/*`
- reports and runtime JSON under `reports/*`

Current state surfaces include:

- issue records
- lease records
- retry and cooldown metadata
- finalization state
- integration queue and lock
- worktree state
- global reconciler values
- evidence and reporting artifacts

## Current git and branch behavior

The current runtime uses:

- long-lived named worktrees
- per-worktree branches
- executor-local sync against `origin/main`
- branch publication from runner paths
- cherry-pick based integration in the integrator
- bounded non-publishing worktree reset in the recovery daemon

The key remaining git risk is outside Workstreams A and C: main-repo boundary exceptions and broader state ownership still need hardening in later workstreams.

# Current Control Plane And Flows

## Current control-plane actors

The current platform has these control-plane actors:

- `linear-webhook-receiver`
- `discord-request-router`
- `symphony-agent-router`
- `symphony-scheduler`
- `linear-reconciler`
- `symphony-runner`
- `symphony-queue-control`
- `symphony-integrator`
- `symphony-worktree-recovery`
- `bridge-watchdog`
- `worktree-health`

Not all of them should own scheduling or git mutation.

After Workstreams A and C, only the scheduler owns global Linear claims, and recovery no longer publishes code.

## Current Linear flow

1. Linear changes state or emits an event.
2. `linear-webhook-receiver` decides whether the event is eligible.
3. It writes desired-work ingress.
4. The scheduler discovers eligible work from Linear state and desired-work signals.
5. The scheduler claims the issue durably and assigns a worktree.
6. The scheduler posts to `/v1/linear/trigger` on the Symphony router.
7. The router verifies the scheduler-owned claim and forwards to the assigned executor.
8. The runner syncs the worktree from `origin/main`.
9. The runner acquires a lease heartbeat and starts work.
10. Validation and finalization run.
11. The runner may publish branch state.
12. The integrator later cherry-picks into `main`.

## Current reconciler flow

`linear-reconciler` does all of the following:

- checks healthy capacity
- inspects queue depth
- feeds Todo from Backlog
- detects stale work
- re-enqueues stale integration candidates
- writes desired-work signals for scheduler attention

This means it is now a feeder and repair input, not a direct dispatcher.

## Current runner flow

The runner currently does all of the following:

- syncs the worktree from `origin/main` before lease acquisition
- fetches issue detail for an explicitly assigned issue or sticky repair
- acquires and heartbeats a lease
- runs AI work
- validates results
- may commit and push worktree branch state
- updates Linear state and comments
- emits completion and retry metadata

The runner is now an executor only for global Linear work. It does not self-pick runnable issues from Linear state.

## Current recovery flow

The worktree recovery daemon currently does all of the following:

- scans all worktrees
- classifies them
- releases stale leases
- sets worktree state
- quarantines or reprovisions unsafe sandboxes
- performs bounded non-publishing sandbox maintenance for `reset_to_main` on inactive diverged worktrees
- runs detect-only baseline health checks and reports cspell failures for operator intervention

Recovery no longer auto-commits, pushes, or propagates git state. Its remaining filesystem mutation is limited to non-publishing sandbox reset of inactive worktrees.

## Current integration flow

The integrator is already single-writer by intent:

- reads integration queue
- acquires integration lock
- cherry-picks candidate branch head onto `main`
- reports success or conflict

This remains the most correct part of the control plane and is now fed by a more stable upstream claim model than before.

## Why the previous flow was unsafe

The system previously mixed three patterns:

- edge-triggered webhook dispatch
- level-triggered backlog reconciliation
- worker-local self-pick

That combination was unsafe when all three could touch the same queue without an earlier authoritative claim. Workstream A removed that split global scheduling model.

## Current execution classes

The runtime still does not fully separate three classes of work:

- read-only
- command-only
- mutating

Production design must continue to treat them differently.

Read-only and command-only tasks should not pay the full repository mutation cost.

Mutating tasks must go through the full state, validation, and integration pipeline.

# Known Failures And Evidence

## Summary

The current failures are structural.

Provider rate limits, individual AI errors, and flaky tasks exist, but they are not the main reason the harness behaves unpredictably.

## Evidence-backed failure list

| Failure | Current evidence | Current mechanism | Required correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duplicate Linear dispatch | Router logs show the same issue dispatched to more than one worktree. Example: `ANQ-1580` was sent to `wt1` and `wt2` within about one second. | Webhook and reconciler both triggered dispatch before a durable claim existed. | Create an atomic claim before dispatch and make one scheduler authoritative per repo. |
| Repeated replay of the same issue | Router and reconciler logs show repeated redispatch of `ANQ-1617`. | Reconciler re-sees work as eligible because ownership and retry state are not stable enough. | Separate ingress from claim. Reconciler may only requeue expired claims, not redispatch runnable work opportunistically. |
| Lease loss during execution and validation | Integration tests and logs include `lease_mismatch` and abandonment flows. | Lease starts too late and competes with other state mutations. | Move durable claim earlier. Keep lease as execution heartbeat only. |
| Recovery mutates git | `anqr-symphony-worktree-recovery.service` sets `ANQR_AUTOMATION_COMMIT=1` and `ANQR_AUTOMATION_PUSH=1`. Recovery code performs commit, push, sync, and propagation work. | Recovery is acting as a second git writer. | Make recovery state-only. Do not allow background repair to commit, push, merge, or reset active workspaces. |
| Late conflict discovery | Integrator logs show repeated cherry-pick conflicts for `ANQ-1617` before a later success. | Conflict is discovered after local execution, not at claim or candidate admission time. | Make candidate admission explicit and repo-serial. Treat base SHA drift as a first-class invalidation rule. |
| Split scheduling authority | Webhook, reconciler, runner self-pick, queue control, and recovery all influence runnable work. | The control plane is split. | Introduce one repo-scoped scheduler with exclusive claim authority. |
| Capacity is advisory, not authoritative | Router chooses least-loaded worktree using local `activeRequests`. | Local request counters do not prove issue ownership. | Capacity decisions must consume durable claim state, not only in-memory request counters. |
| Worktrees drift and get repaired under load | Recovery and runner both sync or repair against `origin/main`. | Worktree baseline can move under or between executions. | Idle worktrees may refresh. Active worktrees must stay pinned to claim base until completion or expiry. |
| Tests miss the control-plane failure mode | Current tests verify webhook ingress, worktree creation, and some lease-loss behavior. They do not prove scheduler exclusivity under concurrent ingress. | Tests prove local intent, not distributed correctness. | Add duplicate-dispatch, split-brain, restart, conflict, and lease-expiry concurrency tests. |

## Current nonconformances that must be documented openly

### The system is not effectively once

The current runtime is not effectively-once for mutating Linear work.

It is at best at-least-once with manual cleanup.

### Ancillary services are not ancillary enough

`linear-reconciler`, `symphony-worktree-recovery`, and parts of runner behavior are shaping execution ownership and git state.

That violates the intended model where executors do work and support services only recover from failure.

### Worktree identity is overloaded

A worktree currently represents:

- a pool slot
- a long-lived branch
- a mutable sandbox
- a repair surface
- a possible durable owner of issue progress

Those roles should be split.

### Existing documentation mixed intent with remediation

Previous docs often described a desired state as if it already existed.

This set replaces that with explicit status labeling.

# Production Target Architecture

## Design objective

The target design must allow:

- parallel execution across many tasks
- exact or effective once claiming per repository
- safe merge-back
- clean propagation of upstream changes
- bounded retries
- reliable recovery
- full auditability

## Recommended control-plane model

Use a **repo-scoped authoritative scheduler**.

Per repository, the system must have:

- one ingress-normalization path
- one scheduler with exclusive claim authority
- one execution lease model
- one integration queue
- one integration writer

## Authoritative ownership boundaries

### Ingress

Ingress may:

- accept events
- normalize payloads
- dedupe delivery IDs
- classify work as read-only, command-only, or mutating
- write desired work into durable state

Ingress may not:

- choose the final executor
- grant durable ownership
- mutate repository state

### Scheduler

Scheduler may:

- compute eligible jobs
- reserve capacity
- create claims atomically
- assign a worker pool and executor
- requeue expired claims

Scheduler must be the only actor allowed to transition:

- `eligible -> claimed`

### Executor

Executor may:

- pull or receive a claimed job
- create a task sandbox
- heartbeat the lease
- run AI work and tools
- run quality gates
- emit candidate artifacts or branch state

Executor may not:

- decide global queue ownership
- integrate directly to `main`

### Integrator

Integrator may:

- read candidate queue
- verify base SHA and validation status
- merge or cherry-pick one candidate at a time per repo
- mark conflict, stale-base, or integrated outcomes

Integrator must be the only writer to the repository mainline.

### Recovery

Recovery may:

- detect dead workers
- expire claims
- requeue work
- quarantine sandboxes
- request reprovisioning

Recovery may not:

- commit
- push
- fast-forward
- rebase active sandboxes
- reset active sandboxes
- merge mainline changes into active sandboxes

## Recommended execution classes

### Read-only

Examples:

- simple questions
- repository search
- file counting
- explanation tasks

Policy:

- no integration path
- no branch publication
- no worktree required unless tools require repository access
- fast timeout and cheap retry

### Command-only

Examples:

- controlled shell commands
- diagnostics
- report generation

Policy:

- no integration path unless explicitly configured to persist artifacts
- sandbox required if filesystem mutation is possible
- evidence required when operator-visible outputs matter

### Mutating

Examples:

- file edits
- test additions
- refactors
- service file changes
- documentation updates

Policy:

- claim required before execution
- sandbox required
- pinned base SHA required
- quality gate policy required
- candidate admission required
- repo-serial integration required

## Recommended merge strategy

Use one of these two equivalent shapes:

- patch artifact submission to a single integrator
- task branch submission to a single integrator

In both cases:

- the executor does not update `main`
- the candidate records its base SHA
- the integrator decides admission against current `main`
- conflicts become explicit states, not silent resets

## Recommended stale work rules

- a claim is stale only after heartbeat expiry plus grace
- a candidate is stale if its base SHA no longer satisfies integration policy
- an active sandbox is invalid only when its claim expires or the operator cancels it
- upstream `main` movement does not justify background mutation of an active sandbox

## Multi-repo design

For multi-repo support, keep the same control-plane model but scope it per repo:

- claim namespace per repo
- executor pool mapping per repo
- integration queue per repo
- integration lock per repo

Cross-repo work becomes a parent job that coordinates child repo jobs with explicit dependency edges.

## Constraints for worktree viability

A worktree-based executor pool remains viable only if all of these are true:

- worktrees are sandboxes, not durable source of truth
- active worktrees are not background-mutated
- only the scheduler owns task claims
- only the integrator writes mainline
- worktree refresh happens only when idle or when the sandbox is reprovisioned

Without those constraints, the current worktree-first model is not reliable.

# State Machines

## Why state machines matter

The harness currently has state, but the transitions are not strict enough.

Production behavior requires explicit state machines for jobs, claims, candidates, and sandboxes.

## Job lifecycle

### Read-only and command-only jobs

`received -> normalized -> eligible -> claimed -> executing -> completed`

Failure branches:

- `retry_wait`
- `failed`
- `dead_letter`

### Mutating jobs

`received -> normalized -> eligible -> claimed -> executing -> validation_pending -> candidate_ready -> integrating -> integrated`

Failure branches:

- `validation_failed`
- `stale_claim`
- `conflict`
- `retry_wait`
- `manual_review`
- `dead_letter`

## Claim lifecycle

`none -> claimed -> active -> expired -> released`

Required claim fields:

- `jobId`
- `repoId`
- `claimId`
- `executionAttemptId`
- `workerId`
- `pool`
- `claimedAt`
- `leaseExpiresAt`
- `baseSha`
- `jobClass`

## Lease lifecycle

`created -> heartbeating -> expired`

Lease exists to protect active execution.

Lease does not replace ingress dedupe or atomic claim.

## Candidate lifecycle

`none -> candidate_ready -> integrating -> integrated`

Failure branches:

- `conflict`
- `stale_base`
- `rejected`
- `manual_review`

Required candidate fields:

- `integrationCandidateId`
- `repoId`
- `jobId`
- `claimId`
- `baseSha`
- `candidateHeadSha`
- `changedPaths`
- `validationSummary`
- `createdAt`

## Worktree or sandbox lifecycle

`idle -> provisioned -> executing -> awaiting_disposal -> disposed`

Failure branches:

- `quarantined`
- `reprovisioning`

A sandbox is not an owner record.

It is disposable execution infrastructure.

## Current mismatch against target

The current runtime mixes issue state, lease state, worktree state, and finalization state, but still allows:

- external redispatch before claim
- recovery-driven mutation of git
- requeue without strong attempt identity
- late conflict discovery

The target model fixes that by making each transition authoritative and singular.

# Worktree And Git Governance

## Current worktree policy

The current fleet uses eight long-lived worktrees:

- `wt1` to `wt4` for Linear
- `wt5` to `wt8` for Discord

That split is acceptable as a pool definition.

It is not acceptable as a durable ownership model.

## Required worktree policy

### What a worktree is

A worktree is:

- an executor sandbox
- a filesystem and git isolation boundary
- a disposable pool slot

A worktree is not:

- a durable source of task truth
- the authoritative scheduler state
- the recovery authority
- a reason to mutate other active worktrees

## Refresh rules

### Allowed

- refresh idle worktrees from `origin/main`
- reprovision quarantined worktrees
- discard completed task sandboxes
- rehydrate a fresh sandbox for a retry attempt

### Forbidden

- fast-forward active worktrees under an active claim
- merge `main` into active worktrees in the background
- auto-commit dirty active worktrees from recovery
- push active worktree branches from recovery
- reset active worktrees because another branch integrated

## Branch and base rules

Every mutating attempt must record:

- repository
- branch or patch identity
- base SHA
- execution attempt ID

Every integration attempt must compare candidate base SHA to current mainline state.

## Conflict policy

When two mutating jobs overlap in the same repository:

- both may execute in parallel
- only one candidate may integrate at a time
- later candidates must be checked against the new base
- conflict becomes an explicit state
- the platform must not hide the conflict with reset-and-retry loops

## Invalidating stale work

A task becomes stale when:

- its claim expires
- its worker dies and heartbeat grace elapses
- its candidate cannot satisfy current integration policy
- an operator cancels it

A task does not become stale merely because:

- another task integrated first
- recovery decided to resync the pool
- queue depth changed

## Multi-repo rule

If the platform expands beyond one repo, each repo needs its own:

- scheduler state
- integration queue
- integration lock
- sandbox pool policy

Cross-repo work must be coordinated above the repo layer, not by sharing one blind scheduler loop.

# Quality Gates And Post-AI Processing

## Purpose

Post-AI processing is mandatory for any mutating task.

The executor is not done when the model stops. It is done when the work has been validated, evidenced, and admitted for integration.

## Gate tiers from the current repository

### Base repository gates

The current repository exposes these important gate surfaces:

- `make quality-fast`
- `make quality-release`
- `make quality-harness`
- `make quality-full`

The current script layer also exposes targeted commands such as:

- `npm run typecheck:harness`
- `npm run lint:harness`
- `npm run depcruise:harness`
- `npm run test:unit`
- `npm run queue:all:dry-run`
- `npm run linear:reconciler:once`
- `npm run harness:doctor`

## Required gate policy by task class

### Read-only

Required:

- no repository gates
- response evidence only when operator requested or when the task informs later action

### Command-only

Required:

- command exit status
- output capture
- any relevant diagnostics
- no integration path unless artifacts are intentionally persisted

### Mutating harness work

For changes touching `harness/*`, `services/systemd/*`, or `docs/harness/*`, the default minimum policy is:

1. targeted repo validation
   - `npm run typecheck:harness`
   - `npm run lint:harness`
   - `npm run depcruise:harness`
2. baseline regression
   - `npm run test:unit`
3. harness dry-run checks when orchestration logic changed
   - `make quality-harness`

For broader or cross-cutting repository changes, the candidate admission policy should escalate to:

- `make quality-fast`

For release-grade change sets or production rollout work, candidate admission should escalate to:

- `make quality-full`

## Evidence required after mutating work

Every candidate must record:

- commands run
- pass or fail result for each command
- changed paths
- base SHA
- candidate SHA
- integration decision
- rollback note or conflict note
- follow-up required

## Current gap

The current harness has evidence generation and gate surfaces, but it does not yet enforce a clean candidate admission policy before merge-back.

That policy is mandatory for production.

# Observability And Audit

## Current strength

The current runtime already logs a lot of useful detail:

- service identity
- worktree identity
- queue and dispatch events
- some correlation IDs
- issue transitions
- integration attempts
- recovery actions

That is enough to infer major failures.

## Current weakness

It is still too hard to prove the exact causal chain for one job across ingress, claim, execution, recovery, and integration.

## Required audit fields

Every job needs these identifiers:

- `job_id`
- `source_event_id`
- `correlation_id`
- `claim_id`
- `execution_attempt_id`
- `integration_candidate_id`
- `integration_attempt_id`
- `repo_id`
- `worker_id`
- `sandbox_id`
- `worktree_id` when applicable

## Required logs

### Ingress

Log:

- original source
- normalized job class
- dedupe decision
- repo selection
- desired work record created

### Claim and scheduler

Log:

- claim creation
- actor creating claim
- capacity decision
- pool selection
- worktree or sandbox selection
- duplicate claim rejection

### Executor

Log:

- base SHA at start
- current HEAD at start
- worker and sandbox identity
- heartbeat renewals
- validation steps
- candidate emission

### Recovery

Log:

- stale detection reason
- worker liveness check
- state transition performed
- proof that no git mutation occurred

### Integrator

Log:

- candidate selected
- base SHA
- current mainline SHA
- merge or cherry-pick result
- conflict files
- integrated SHA

## Required metrics

- duplicate dispatch attempts
- duplicate claim rejections
- claim expiries
- lease mismatches
- validation failures
- integration conflicts
- stale-base rejections
- retries by issue
- quarantined sandboxes
- recovery actions by type
- mean queue age
- integration latency
- pool utilization by class

## Current audit gaps that must be closed

- no single authoritative claim record before dispatch
- no universal attempt ID threaded through all services
- too much reliance on local request counters
- no strong proof that recovery did not mutate active jobs
- no explicit candidate admission audit contract

# Operations Runbooks

## Principle

Operational safety comes before throughput.

When the control plane is under repair, disable mutation and keep read-only and diagnostic work separate.

## Runbook: controlled restart of routing or executor services

1. stop new mutating work admission
2. wait for active claims to drain or expire cleanly
3. verify no candidate is mid-integration
4. restart the target service
5. confirm health endpoints
6. resume admission

Current helper scripts such as `harness/ops/orchestration/symphony-control.mjs` may remain useful, but service restart must follow the claim and integration state, not only timer state.

## Runbook: duplicate execution suspected

1. identify the issue identifier
2. inspect scheduler, ingress, and router logs for duplicate trigger events
3. identify all claim or attempt records
4. cancel all but the authoritative claim
5. quarantine any sandbox with ambiguous mutation history
6. document the duplicate-dispatch root cause

## Runbook: stale lease

1. confirm worker heartbeat loss
2. confirm worker process liveness
3. expire claim after grace
4. requeue the job as a new attempt
5. preserve old attempt evidence
6. do not mutate the old sandbox in place unless it is explicitly quarantined and isolated

## Runbook: integration conflict

1. capture candidate metadata and conflicting paths
2. mark candidate `conflict`
3. do not reset the sandbox into a new hidden state
4. create a replan or manual-review path
5. admit no silent auto-merge claim

## Runbook: quarantined sandbox

1. preserve audit metadata
2. capture changed paths and current HEAD
3. remove from scheduling pool
4. reprovision a fresh sandbox
5. only requeue the job if the claim is no longer active and retry policy allows it

## Runbook: provider failure

1. classify provider failure
2. keep job ownership stable
3. retry inside provider policy if claim is still valid
4. do not re-dispatch the same job to another executor without expiring or releasing the claim first

## Runbook: Discord read-only degradation

If mutating repo work is disabled, Discord may still serve:

- read-only questions
- diagnostics
- documentation lookup
- repository search

That mode must be declared clearly in operator status.

# Validation And Rollout Plan

## Goal

Prove the architecture is correct before trusting it with unattended mutating work.

## Required validation suites

### Duplicate-dispatch suite

Prove:

- webhook and reconciler can fire together
- only one claim is created
- all later claim attempts are rejected cleanly

### Lease-expiry suite

Prove:

- worker heartbeat loss expires the claim once
- recovery requeues state without mutating git
- retries create a new execution attempt

### Integration-conflict suite

Prove:

- two overlapping candidates can execute in parallel
- only one integrates first
- the other becomes `conflict` or `stale_base`
- no hidden reset converts conflict into fake success

### Restart suite

Prove:

- restarting webhook, router, scheduler, integrator, or recovery does not duplicate an active claim
- integration queue survives restart
- idle sandboxes refresh safely after restart

### Multi-repo suite

If multi-repo support is planned, prove:

- repo A integration conflict does not block repo B
- claims are unique within repo scope
- cross-repo parent jobs respect dependency order

## Rollout stages

### Stage 1

- documentation and state-machine alignment
- control-plane authority reduction
- recovery changed to state-only behavior

### Stage 2

- atomic claim before dispatch
- candidate admission contract
- repo-serial integration enforcement

### Stage 3

- concurrency and failure-injection tests
- operator dashboards and metrics
- dry-run shadow execution

### Stage 4

- limited mutating production rollout
- bounded issue classes only
- explicit incident review after every conflict, duplicate, or stale-claim event

## Exit criteria for production

The mutating platform is production ready only when all of these hold:

- zero duplicate claims in forced-concurrency tests
- zero background git mutation by recovery
- one writer to mainline per repo
- full audit chain from event to integration
- deterministic recovery after restart
